To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
random-sequence genetic pools can spontaneously recombine, and the chemical constitution of genetic polymers determines the extent of recombination.
random-sequence RNA and AtNA pools display an innate capacity for spontaneous recombination, which promotes an increase in compositional and informational complexity.

the vicinal cis-diol configuration of the ribose and altritol sugars of RNA and AtNA, respectively, endows the corresponding genetic polymer pools with a spontaneous propensity for intermolecular recombina- tion, which promotes a concomitant rise in compositional, information and structural pool complexity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chemical origins of life and the emergence of biological information, and we propose that the chemical reactivity of genetic polymers is a key factor in their evolutionary potential.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the chemical constitution that makes RNA susceptible to hydrolytic degradation also makes it susceptible to recombination, which in turn makes RNA susceptible to evolution.

the chemical constitution that enables RNA and AtNA to undergo hydrolytic cleavage also enables recombination, and that recombination in these systems promotes an increase in compositional and informational pool complexity.

the innate potential for recombination is a fundamental property of genetic polymers, and that the chemical constitution of a genetic polymer is the fundamental determinant of its propensity for recombination.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a fundamental property of genetic polymers is their capacity for non- enzymatic recombination, and that this property is shared between RNA and AtNA, but not between DNA, HNA and ANA, which is mechanistically linked to their different chemical constitutions.
a random-sequence genetic polymer pool can spontaneously recombine, and that the vicinal ring diol configuration of the genetic polymer strand is a key determinant for this process.
a fundamental chemical property of RNA and AtNA, namely the cis-diol configuration, is sufficient to promote non-enzymatically driven recombination and hence evolutionary potential.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the capacity for recombination is an inherent property of the chemical structure of genetic polymers and not a property of dedicated recombinase machinery.
recombination is not an exclusive property of biological systems but is also an intrinsic feature of genetic polymers.
recombination, a fundamental biological process, is not necessarily mediated by dedicated enzymes, but can emerge as an inherent property of genetic polymers.
